title: Acoustic Drone Detection with CNN Spectrogram Analysis
caption: Recognizing drones from their acoustic signatures.
description: An exploration of detecting drones from sound by converting recordings into spectrograms and using a convolutional neural network to recognize acoustic patterns.
note: Project details, training data, and measured performance will be added as the work develops. The cover is an illustrative concept image.
imageAlt: Concept image of a quadcopter above a dark mountain valley, with spectral light patterns suggesting its acoustic signature.

sections.title: Problem
paragraphs: Can a drone be recognized from its acoustic signature? This project explores sound as a source of evidence for drone detection.

sections.title: Scope
paragraphs: The intended task is to distinguish drone audio from other sounds using spectrogram representations. Dataset scope and recording conditions are still to be documented.

sections.title: Approach
paragraphs: Convert audio into spectrograms and use a convolutional neural network to learn patterns associated with drone sound. The representation and model choices will be documented alongside the implementation.

media.alt: Concept image of a quadcopter above a dark mountain valley, with spectral light patterns suggesting its acoustic signature.
media.caption: Concept cover; the spectral light patterns are illustrative, not recorded data.

sections.title: Implementation plan
paragraphs: Develop the audio preprocessing and classification pipeline, then document the training setup and the decisions behind it.

sections.title: Evaluation plan
paragraphs: Evaluate on held-out recordings and report both successful detections and errors. Measured results will be added when available.

sections.title: Next steps
paragraphs: Define the recording dataset, establish a baseline, and test how well the model handles variation in background sound.

title: Academic Advising RAG Chatbot
caption: Academic questions, grounded in source documents.
description: A retrieval-augmented chatbot for academic-advising questions, using relevant catalog, curriculum, and policy documents to ground its responses.
note: The intended focus is clear answers with traceable sources. Supported documents, implementation details, and evaluation will be added as the project develops. The cover is a concept image.
imageAlt: Concept image of academic books, course documents, and a laptop showing abstract conversation and source-document cards on a warm ivory desk.

title: 2D Lightning Simulation with a Probabilistic Potential Model
caption: Exploring how local probabilities grow branching discharges.
description: A two-dimensional lightning simulation that explores branching discharge paths through a probabilistic potential model.
note: The project will document the potential model, growth rules, and the patterns they produce. The cover is an illustrative concept image rather than a simulation result.
imageAlt: Concept visualization of a planar branching electrical discharge, with fine blue-white filaments against a deep indigo field.

title: Art
caption: Acrylic, ink, printmaking, and watercolor. Mostly birds.
description: Until I compiled this collection of some of my more polished pieces some time ago, I did not realize that I had been so invested in creating birds. A part of this is definitely because in the past my family has had several pet chickens, and I really enjoyed spending time with them.
note: Recently, I’ve been more interested in getting good at drawing people. (But until then, look at these birds!)
imageAlt: A black-and-white overprint of layered textbook pages, illustrations, equations, and diagrams.

media.alt: A photograph of a square acrylic painting: a blue and black Steller’s jay rendered in dots against a fiery orange and yellow background.

paragraphs: This is an acrylic painting of a Steller’s jay. Having been camping in certain parts of California, I’ve been woken up by these guys quite a few times.
Something I find interesting about them, and

paragraphs.text: all blue birds for that matter

paragraphs: , is that their feathers contain no blue
. Instead of absorbing non-blue colors and reflecting what remains, they manipulate and refract light in a way that produces blue frequencies of light.
They’re quite eye-catching, and I think that the sharp point they have on the back of their heads is funny.
The technique used here is called
, and you’d more often see it done with ink in black & white, but I like the effect it produces.

media.alt: A framed painting of a chicken made from curved broken strokes of green, brown, cream, and orange over a contrasting red background.

paragraphs: This Chicken looks quite like one I’ve had in the past. The breed is something between an “
” and an “Americana,” depending on who you ask.
Why does the painting look so …? This is a technique called
. By first creating an underlayer of a
inverse color (in terms of the color wheel), you can really make the colors pop through that almost violent contrast.
This was quite hard to get right and I was worried throughout the process what the end result would be, but it came out better than I expected.

media.alt: An ink drawing of a chicken on white paper with a blue border; dense hatching defines its feathers and the shadow around its feet.

paragraphs: Well, here’s another chicken. Same deal as before with the breed. This time, though, it has been depicted in ink using a process called
Something you may not think about if you’ve never studied art, is that the goal, even when practicing (maybe
when practicing), is
usually to depict the subject as “accurately” as possible.

The brain is actually pretty lazy, and our eyes do stuff without us noticing all the time. Look around the legs of the chicken: the shadow has artificially been darkened to make the legs appear lighter relative to the background. With this contrast, you can tell what is happening where it otherwise might have been more ambiguous. The same is done in the other direction with light tones.

media.alt: A carved rubber bird stamp on a table above three black bird prints on green, pink, and purple paper.

paragraphs: This one is pretty self explanatory: it’s a rubber stamp. There’s not really any undos when it comes to making something in this way, but maybe that’s part of the appeal. I thought it was fun to make!
